slides.title:
Client paid
late again?
slides.sub:
The 4 emails to send,
and exactly when.

slides.title:
Same day:
send the invoice
slides.text: Send it the day you deliver, while the work is fresh. Always put a due date on it.
slides.box: Due within 14 days of the invoice date.
slides.label: PASTE THIS LINE

slides.title:
1–3 days late:
a friendly nudge
slides.text: Keep it light. Most late invoices are just forgotten.
slides.box: “In case it got lost in your inbox, here it is again.”
slides.label: TRY THIS

slides.title:
About 10 days late:
ask for a date
slides.text: Ask when you can expect the payment. Offer to fix the invoice if something is wrong.
slides.box: “Could you let me know when I can expect it?”
slides.label: TRY THIS

slides.title:
3+ weeks late:
final notice
slides.text: Give one new date. Say that ongoing work pauses until the invoice is paid.
slides.box: Calm and clear. No guilt, no drama.
slides.label: TONE

slides.title:
Let your tracker
count the days
slides.text: Every invoice counts its own late days, so you always know which email is next.

bullets: Invoices that count their late days
Clients, proposals, projects and invoices in one place

carousels.caption:
Client paid late again? Here is what to send, and when:

1. Same day: send the invoice with a due date
2. 1–3 days late: a friendly nudge
3. About 10 days late: ask for a payment date
4. 3+ weeks late: a calm final notice
5. Let your tracker count the late days

Save this for the next late client, and send it to a freelancer friend who needs it.

slides.title:
You send it
and wait
slides.text: Most clients need a nudge. Follow up 3 days after you send, then about a week later.

slides.title: No expiry date
slides.text: Give every quote a “valid until” date. It gives the client a reason to decide.

slides.title:
Your price
is a guess
slides.text: Hours × your rate. If the quote is lower than that, you priced too low.

slides.title:
You never ask
why you lost
slides.text: One short question after a “no” tells you what to fix: price, timing or scope.
slides.box: “Could I ask what made you decide? It helps me get better.”
slides.label: TRY THIS

slides.title:
Your pipeline lives
in your head
slides.text: Put every quote on one board, from Draft to Won or Lost.

bullets: A next step on every quote
Warns you before a quote expires

carousels.caption:

1. You send it and wait: follow up after 3 days, then a week later

3. Your price is a guess: check hours × your rate
4. You never ask why you lost
5. Your pipeline lives in your head
